setting.name: Disable UAC (Full)
setting.casual_explanation: This fully disables User Account Control by forcing the main EnableLUA switch off.
setting.why_people_change_it: People only do this when they want to remove UAC prompts entirely, usually on specialized lab or gaming systems, and they accept the security downside.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Turning UAC fully off removes an important Windows security boundary and normally requires a reboot to take full effect. The app behavior is clear, but provenance still treats this as a review-only card rather than a fully curated research preset.
setting.professional_notes: The live app models this card as a command-backed registry tweak that queries HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\EnableLUA, applies EnableLUA = 0, and restores the previously detected value or deletes the value when it was originally missing. Repo security docs list the same card, but tweak provenance and tweak-provenance-missing still mark it as category-fallback pending a stronger tweak-specific upstream repo match.
